Our story

A better path should be easier to find.

Higher education can change a life. Understanding how to get there should not require becoming an expert in transfer policy.

It started with real degree plans.

The idea behind DegreeSteps grew from our founder’s family experience. Our founder earned a BSBA from Thomas Edison State University, an MBA from Purdue Global, and a DBA from South College, and reports completing that education without student debt. Transfer credit and self-paced learning were important parts of the journey.

Another family plan brought three years of prior college work into a residential Liberty program, creating a path to finish the remaining year on campus. These are personal experiences shared by the founder—not a promise that another student will receive the same awards, price, or timeline.

When friends asked for similar help, the recurring obstacle was clear: useful options already existed, but finding and combining them into a reliable plan was complicated.

Make the options understandable.

DegreeSteps brings the moving pieces together: a student’s goal, a receiving school’s rules, original learning records, outside-credit sources, and the work that remains. The aim is a simple experience with enough detail to support an informed next step.

Some students want an online degree as efficiently as possible. Others value a campus experience, a particular institution, a career change, or the preparation required for a licensed profession. A useful plan must respect those motivations.

Build knowledge together.

Students can learn from one another’s plans, questions, and reported outcomes. Community contributions help identify practical opportunities and policies that deserve a closer look. Evidence and receiving-school decisions remain distinct from votes and popularity.

We want better information to become easier to find and easier to use, so more people can move forward with confidence.

Keep the promise practical.

We do not need to pretend every school is fully mapped to be useful. DegreeSteps labels partial research, missing prices, conditional course matches, and unresolved questions. The next useful action may be choosing a source—or asking the school for a decision first.
